**About Us:**

Since 1991, Pajaro Valley Prevention and Student Assistance (PVPSA) has supported the health and well-being of youth and families throughout the Pajaro Valley. The organization provides comprehensive health education, mental health services, substance use prevention and intervention, and direct counseling to students and families, including those served by the Pajaro Valley Unified School District (PVUSD), the largest school district in Santa Cruz County and extending into North Monterey County.

PVPSA pioneered a dedicated nonprofit-agency model built around its unique partnership with the local school district. Over more than three decades, the organization has expanded its partnerships across cities, counties, and public and private organizations to address critical community issues including substance use, gang prevention, mental health, school expulsions, and educational outcomes.

At the heart of PVPSA’s work is a commitment to prevention and early intervention. Using an upstream public health approach, the organization works to address the social determinants of health and strengthen community health and wellness through direct services, prevention and intervention programs, community partnerships, and health-related public policy advocacy. Today, PVPSA’s dedicated team works alongside schools, families, and community partners to create healthier environments and better outcomes for local youth and families.

**Summary of Position:**

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) serves as PVPSA’s senior executive leader and is responsible for the overall strategic direction, organizational health, financial sustainability, and impact of the organization. The CEO will join PVPSA at an important point in its evolution. This leader will have the opportunity to strengthen organizational infrastructure, cultivate a positive and accountable culture, deepen community relationships, and position PVPSA for long-term sustainability and impact.

The CEO will be a visible and engaged leader both within the organization and throughout the greater Watsonville community. They will work closely with staff, the Board, funders, government partners, school districts, and community stakeholders to advance PVPSA’s mission and ensure the organization remains responsive to the evolving needs of the youth and families it serves.

* Translate organizational strategy into clear priorities, measurable objectives, and actionable plans.
* Provide overall leadership and oversight of PVPSA’s programs, operations, finances, people, and organizational infrastructure.
* Assess organizational needs and strengthen systems, structures, policies, and processes to support PVPSA’s continued effectiveness and sustainability.
* Foster organizational adaptability and guide the team effectively through change, growth, and evolving community needs.
* Identify and proactively manage organizational, operational, financial, and reputational risks.
* Ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, contracts, funding requirements, and organizational policies.

* Foster strong communication and collaboration across programs and functions.
* Build trusted relationships with employees at all levels of the organization and maintain a visible, accessible leadership presence.
* Oversee organizational approaches to talent development, performance management, succession planning, and employee engagement and retention.
* Partner with organizational leaders to ensure effective human resources practices and a positive employee experience.

jobs.description:
**The Organization**

The Mental Health Client Action Network (MHCAN) is a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization dedicated to supporting adults in Santa Cruz County with lived experience of mental health challenges. Founded nearly 40 years ago as an independent peer support center, MHCAN is actively transitioning its operational framework to an accredited Clubhouse Model of Services.

In alignment with Clubhouse standards, MHCAN operates as a member-driven community where participants ("members") and staff work side-by-side to run daily center operations, build social connections, and pursue employment, education, and wellness goals. All MHCAN staff members share lived experience with a mental health condition and/or navigating the mental health system.

**Position Summary**

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of MHCAN and is responsible for providing strategic leadership, operational oversight, program management, community engagement, and resource development. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director ensures the organization stays true to its core mission of peer empowerment while successfully guiding the agency through its transition to the Clubhouse model and maintaining strong alignment with County Behavioral Health.

This is a full-time (1.0 FTE / 40 hours per week) exempt position.

**Compensation:** $95,000 – $105,000 annually, depending on experience.

**Core Responsibilities**

**Human Resources & Staff Leadership (25%)**

* Hire, train, supervise, and mentor all program staff and peer support team members.
* Foster a positive, supportive, and accountable organizational culture centered on lived experience and recovery.
* Manage staff scheduling, performance evaluations, and team development.
* Partner with the Fiscal Agent (FSAS) on HR policy enforcement, workplace safety, and personnel administration.

**Program Oversight & Clubhouse Model Transition (25%)**

* Lead the agency’s transition to and ongoing operation of a certified Clubhouse model of services.
* Ensure daily program activities effectively meet client needs and contract objectives.
* Evaluate program outcomes and implement continuous service delivery improvements.
* Monitor compliance with grant deliverables and County service agreements.

**Organizational Leadership & Strategy (20%)**

* Implement the organization's mission, vision, and strategic goals, serving as a passionate advocate for peer support.
* Develop annual organizational objectives in close collaboration with the Board of Directors and the County contract monitor.
* Ensure organizational compliance with all applicable legal and nonprofit regulatory standards.
* Provide monthly performance, operational, and financial reports to the Board.

**Community Relations & County Partnership (15%)**

* Serve as the primary spokesperson and public representative for MHCAN.
* Build and maintain productive, collaborative relationships with County Behavioral Health, local community partners, and contracted service providers.
* Represent MHCAN in local task forces, community meetings, and mental health advocacy networks.

**Fundraising & Resource Development (10%)**

* Research, write, and manage grant applications to diversify funding streams.
* Cultivate relationships with individual donors, private foundations, and community partners.
* Oversee donor stewardship and track grant reporting deadlines.

**Financial Oversight & Fiscal Agent Coordination (5%)**

* Develop and manage the annual operating budget (approximately $590,000) in partnership with the Board and Fiscal Agent.
* Collaborate directly with Front St. Administrative Services to oversee fiduciary practices, review monthly financial statements, and ensure budget alignment. *(Note: Daily bookkeeping, payroll processing, and accounting entries are performed directly by the Fiscal Agent.)*

  

**Qualifications**

* **Lived Experience:** Lived experience as a person with a mental health condition and/or direct experience navigating the mental health system is required.
* **Education & Experience:** Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent practical experience.
* **Leadership Experience:** Minimum 2–3 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in a nonprofit or community service environment.
* **Management & Budgeting:** Demonstrated experience supervising staff, managing program operations, and overseeing grant/contract deliverables.
* **Skills:** Strong communication, interpersonal, and project management skills with the ability to build consensus across diverse community stakeholders.

**Performance Expectations**

* Maintain a balanced annual budget in coordination with the Fiscal Agent.
* Ensure successful transition and operational implementation of the Clubhouse model.
* Provide consistent leadership, accountability, and support to program staff.
* Maintain strong, transparent relationships with the Board of Directors, County Behavioral Health, and community partners.
* Ensure timely completion of grant reports and contract deliverables.

**Working Conditions & Physical Requirements**

* Standard office environment with high levels of interpersonal interaction.
* Computer and telephone usage for extended periods.
* Occasional evening or weekend attendance at Board meetings or community events.
* Local travel within Santa Cruz County.
* Ability to lift up to 25 pounds occasionally.

**Reporting Relationship:** Reports directly to the MHCAN Board of Directors.

jobs.description:
**The Organization**

The Mental Health Client Action Network (MHCAN) is a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization dedicated to supporting adults in Santa Cruz County with lived experience of mental health challenges. Founded nearly 40 years ago as an independent peer support center, MHCAN is actively transitioning its operational framework to an accredited Clubhouse Model of Services.

In alignment with Clubhouse standards, MHCAN operates as a member-driven community where participants ("members") and staff work side-by-side to run daily center operations, build social connections, and pursue employment, education, and wellness goals. All MHCAN staff members share lived experience with a mental health condition and/or navigating the mental health system.

**Position Summary**

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of MHCAN and is responsible for providing strategic leadership, operational oversight, program management, community engagement, and resource development. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director ensures the organization stays true to its core mission of peer empowerment while successfully guiding the agency through its transition to the Clubhouse model and maintaining strong alignment with County Behavioral Health.

This is a full-time (1.0 FTE / 40 hours per week) exempt position.

**Compensation:** $95,000 – $105,000 annually, depending on experience.

**Core Responsibilities**

**Human Resources & Staff Leadership (25%)**

* Hire, train, supervise, and mentor all program staff and peer support team members.

* Lead the agency’s transition to and ongoing operation of a certified Clubhouse model of services.
* Ensure daily program activities effectively meet client needs and contract objectives.

* Monitor compliance with grant deliverables and County service agreements.

* Develop annual organizational objectives in close collaboration with the Board of Directors and the County contract monitor.

* Provide monthly performance, operational, and financial reports to the Board.

* Serve as the primary spokesperson and public representative for MHCAN.
* Build and maintain productive, collaborative relationships with County Behavioral Health, local community partners, and contracted service providers.
* Represent MHCAN in local task forces, community meetings, and mental health advocacy networks.

**Fundraising & Resource Development (10%)**

* Research, write, and manage grant applications to diversify funding streams.
* Cultivate relationships with individual donors, private foundations, and community partners.
* Oversee donor stewardship and track grant reporting deadlines.

**Qualifications**

* **Lived Experience:** Lived experience as a person with a mental health condition and/or direct experience navigating the mental health system is required.
* **Education & Experience:** Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent practical experience.
* **Leadership Experience:** Minimum 2–3 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in a nonprofit or community service environment.
* **Management & Budgeting:** Demonstrated experience supervising staff, managing program operations, and overseeing grant/contract deliverables.
* **Skills:** Strong communication, interpersonal, and project management skills with the ability to build consensus across diverse community stakeholders.

**Performance Expectations**

* Maintain a balanced annual budget in coordination with the Fiscal Agent.
* Ensure successful transition and operational implementation of the Clubhouse model.
* Provide consistent leadership, accountability, and support to program staff.
* Maintain strong, transparent relationships with the Board of Directors, County Behavioral Health, and community partners.
* Ensure timely completion of grant reports and contract deliverables.

**Working Conditions & Physical Requirements**

* Standard office environment with high levels of interpersonal interaction.
* Computer and telephone usage for extended periods.
* Occasional evening or weekend attendance at Board meetings or community events.
* Local travel within Santa Cruz County.
* Ability to lift up to 25 pounds occasionally.

**Reporting Relationship:** Reports directly to the MHCAN Board of Directors.

**About the Role**

Dorchester Bay Economic Development Corporation (DBEDC) is hiring a Chief Operating Officer (COO) to lead the organization's internal management and serve as second in command. The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) sets direction and the standard for the organization and leads it externally. The COO makes that direction and standard real inside the organization by managing the six department leads, running the operating rhythm, leading executive-level projects, and translating where DBEDC is going into what it means for each department and for staff day-to-day.

The COO joins an Executive Leadership Team with two peers: the Chief Real Estate Officer, who leads real estate development and asset management, and the Chief Development and Communications Officer, who leads resource development and communications. The three Chiefs work as equals and as thought partners to one another and to the CEO. Much of DBEDC's most important work sits where their areas meet, and the COO is expected to build strong working relationships with both from the start.

Dorchester Bay is a dual-certified community development corporation and community development financial institution serving Dorchester, Roxbury, and nearby neighborhoods. We have about 30 staff, a roughly $10 million operating budget, more than 1000 units of affordable housing, and a community loan fund that finances small businesses and real estate in our neighborhoods. We are a small organization with a large footprint, and our management structure needs to catch up to our complexity.

**Why this role now:**

The Board recently adopted three strategic priorities: Expand Community Ownership and Wealth; Advance Housing as a Platform for Health; and Reframe Education as a Wealth and Power Building Tool and Prepare Residents for the Future Economy. Delivering on them requires an internal leader who can turn priorities into operating plans and hold the organization to them.

Community Engagement, Workforce Development, and Community Lending need to function as one economic stabilization and mobility engine for our neighborhoods rather than as separate lines of work.

Every senior leader currently reports to the CEO. That is too many direct reports for one person to manage well while also leading strategy, policy, the Board, enterprise finance, and external relationships. Our department leads deserve consistent executive management: clear expectations, practical coaching, direct feedback, and support in delivering results.

DBEDC is a technology-forward organization. We expect our leaders to use technology and data to work more effectively, to adopt new tools quickly, and to bring their teams along.

**What the COO owns in one year:**

* **The department leads.** The COO manages, coaches, and develops the six department leads. Every lead has outcome goals, a development plan, and a manager who follows through. The COO raises the standard of leadership across the group and works with the CEO to make the decisions necessary to ensure every department is led at the level our residents and partners deserve.

* **The operating rhythm and executive-level projects.** The COO runs the weekly, monthly, and quarterly management cadence, makes sure decisions get made and carried out, and leads the cross-department projects that require executive ownership, including those shared with real estate and development.

* **Translating direction into practice.** The COO turns the direction the CEO sets and the priorities the Board has adopted into practical operating expectations for each department: what each team is expected to deliver, how the work is organized, and how the three program departments work together as one engine.

Department leads own their departments. The Director of Operations owns administrative systems, policies, and day-to-day operations. The Controller owns accounting, controls, and compliance. Program directors own their programs and the practices that connect them. As a general rule, the COO does not backfill department-level management, stepping into a lead's work only to cover an absence. The COO also recognizes when development has run its course and a leadership change is in the organization's best interest, and leads that process fairly and decisively in partnership with People and Culture and the CEO.

**How the Leadership Team Works Together**

The CEO sets the direction and the standard, communicates where the organization is going, and carries DBEDC's relationships with the Board, funders, partners, and the public, along with enterprise financial stewardship and the organization's most consequential risk decisions. The COO presents operating financial performance to the Board's Finance Committee alongside the CEO and develops the finance function's capacity to do so directly over time. The CEO is direct, moves quickly, and holds a high bar for quality, and expects the leadership team to bring the same clarity and care to their own work.

The three Chiefs lead their areas as peers. The Chief Real Estate Officer leads real estate development and asset management. The Chief Development and Communications Officer leads resource development and communications. The COO leads internal management and the program and administrative departments. The Chiefs are expected to think together, plan together, share information freely, and resolve cross-area questions directly with one another, bringing to the CEO only what they cannot resolve or where the CEO can add value.

The work overlaps constantly. With the Chief Real Estate Officer, the COO makes sure finance supports development projects and property-level accounting across DBEDC's affiliated entities, connects workforce development to jobs created through construction and property operations, aligns community lending with small businesses that lease space in our properties, and makes sure community engagement supports community input on new development.

**The Foundation**

We are the largest nonprofit fighting poverty, disease, and inequity around the world. Founded on a simple premise: people everywhere, regardless of identity or circumstances, should have the chance to live healthy, productive lives. We believe our employees should reflect the rich diversity of the global populations we aim to serve. We provide an exceptional benefits package to employees and their families which include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with no premiums, generous paid time off, paid family leave, foundation-paid retirement contribution, regional holidays, and opportunities to engage in several employee communities. As a workplace, we’re committed to creating an environment for you to thrive both personally and professionally.

**The Team**

Our Global Health (GH) division harnesses advances in science and technology to save lives in poor countries. We focus on the health problems that have a major impact in developing countries but get too little attention and funding. Where tools exist, we support sustainable ways to improve their delivery. Where they don’t, we invest in research and development of new interventions, such as vaccines, drugs, and diagnostics. Our work in infectious diseases focuses on strategies to fight and prevent HIV/AIDS, malaria, tuberculosis (TB), neglected tropical diseases, enteric and diarrheal diseases, pneumonia and maternal, newborn and child health.  
  
Our TB and HIV work is combined under a joint TB/HIV Program Strategy Team (PST) which focuses on research, development and delivery of new products and tools. The foundation’s Tuberculosis (TB) team aims to address key gaps along the TB care pathway through new approaches to protecting against infection, preventing progression from infection to disease, and improving diagnosis and treatment. Our efforts are diversified based on the understanding that vaccines, diagnostics, drugs, and innovative healthcare delivery are all essential to addressing the TB epidemic. Planning and introducing these new tools will be central to our activities.  
  
We focus our HIV efforts on some of the countries hardest hit by HIV in sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in populations at greatest risk of infection, including adolescent girls and young women. While treatment scale-up has led to significant declines in new infections and mortality, the rate is not rapid enough to reach globally agreed targets and there remains a persistently high incidence and mortality in several countries in SSA. The HIV team’s strategic vision is to accelerate the reduction in the incidence of HIV infection in high-burden geographies and populations, with a focus on the development of new and affordable prevention and treatment interventions, including long-acting drugs, vaccines and biologics, and to enable their effective use.

**Your Role**

The TB&HIV Delivery Team is recruiting a Deputy Director, TB Delivery, who will support the Director, HIV & TB Delivery and Program Strategy team (PST) in achieving its impact goals by supporting the development and implementation of the foundation’s HIV & TB Delivery portfolio. As the Deputy Director, you will report to the Director, HIV & TB Delivery and will integrate with key technical/functional colleagues within the team and across the matrix (across teams). Responsibilities will include managing the execution of a growing and complex portfolio of investments in HIV & TB Delivery and focus on strengthening partnerships with global health institutions to meet the PST’s strategic objectives. * Work with members of the TB delivery team and assist them to plan and execute their strategies with fidelity

* Provide strategic guidance in crafting grants and contracts that require research, modeling and analytics

* Lead partnerships with internal and external partners and grantees to advance the foundation’s priorities for TB
* Accountable for the identification and assessment of key portfolio risks and the development and management of mitigation plans
